body: Hi @jstenback, can we add agenda+ to https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585 for this meeting please? There's been some good [discussion](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10378#issuecomment-5604771396) about whether to use `posterfromimg` or an empty `poster-""` to trigger the child img pattern. It'd be good to get agreement there so we can update our spec proposal or not. Also curious on what's needed to proceed to Stage 2. Thanks!
https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12585 is on the agenda now.

Minutes:

- TAC Meeting Agenda and Preparation: Johnny Stenback explained that meeting agendas are sorted automatically by when the "agenda plus" label is added to an issue or pull request ([00:00:05](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.993nijsmmkat)). Additionally, Johnny Stenback reminded participants that the Technical Architecture Committee meeting is approaching in a month and a half, requesting that participants add any relevant topics to the issues list at the top of the meeting notes document so they can coordinate an agenda ([00:02:10](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.bhno15y162y4)).
- PR 12585 Enabled Responsive Images Proposal: Scott Jehl presented pull request 12585 to enable responsive images for video poster elements using a specification proposal reviewed over the past few months ([00:03:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.1fkkpdgsve7j)). Scott Jehl explained the core problem that HTTP archive queries show about 95% of sites use fallback images in video elements that match the poster attribute, but some sites use alternative content or lack opt-ins, risking regressions where fallback text like "your browser doesn't support video" appears as a poster ([00:04:26](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.gwjten5ldt4f)) ([00:08:35](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.j63a1q6gux1b)). To address this, Scott Jehl initially proposed a boolean attribute named `poster from img`, but alternative feedback from Simon Pieters and Anna suggested using an empty `poster` attribute as an opt-in signal, though Scott Jehl noted this would break existing browser support temporarily unless polyfilled ([00:05:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.hxqpk5anm3wc)). Kurt Catti-Schmidt questioned whether an explicit attribute is even necessary given that child images could serve as a direct signal, but Scott Jehl reiterated concerns about pre-existing uses ([00:07:19](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.ob3tusgq9jle)).
- Responsive Images Opt-In Syntax and Precedence: Lea Verou argued that an explicit opt-in on the image element itself (such as using `slot` or a platform-sanctioned equivalent) makes more sense than an attribute on the parent video element, while Simon Pieters presented HTTP archive data showing 22% of pages with an image in a video lacked a poster attribute, confirming that an opt-in like an empty poster attribute is necessary to prevent breaking backwards compatibility ([00:09:42](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.hbryn790kldj)) ([00:12:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.ubu7fneplnbj)). Keith Cirkel and Lea Verou discussed allowing more arbitrary content or custom elements inside the video as a poster, whereas Simon Pieters and Scott Jehl raised complexity, parsing order, and accessibility concerns regarding rich interactive content in poster spaces ([00:15:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.wsdtdsyrjyp7)) ([00:20:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.nl1i1v94stdx)). Ultimately, Scott Jehl and Simon Pieters continued to weigh the trade-offs of an empty poster attribute versus a new opt-in attribute, with Johnny Stenback intervening to encourage continued discussion on the issue tracker ([00:26:15](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.gl951y6dvzky)) ([00:30:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.gy0bxg50w7co)).
- Issue 12861 Navigation History Step Aborts: Shannon Booth raised issue 12861 regarding navigation history steps aborting later cross-document navigation, noting difficulties in reconciling interoperability and test cases across implementations ([00:30:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.gy0bxg50w7co)). Olli Pettay explained that the issue stems from state being set racy and brokenly across the main thread and a parallel queue, noting that Firefox avoids the bug simply by not implementing that specific part of the specification ([00:31:31](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.4qsyikeovp2r)). Jake Archibald and Olli Pettay agreed that since WebKit, Chrome, and Firefox all pass the existing test despite the flawed specification, the specification itself needs to be fixed, prompting Shannon Booth to plan submitting merge requests for feedback ([00:32:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.e0y4qpijvtqj)).
- Issue 11729 HTML Menu Elements Proposal: David Baron requested a status update and more review to advance the HTML menu elements proposal to stage three, noting that responses to checkable menu items and comments from Olli Pettay had been posted in the open UI issue ([00:35:25](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.ql1gljbyd0e2)). Olli Pettay acknowledged the comment and committed to reviewing the proposal the following day ([00:36:30](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.dyj85jolveyo)).
- Issue 10650 HTML and Canvas Rendering and Hit Testing: Philip Jägenstedt and Stefan Zager provided an update on HTML and canvas rendering, noting that captions, subtitles, and video controls will no longer be painted, effectively rendering only media data or the poster element ([00:36:30](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.dyj85jolveyo)). Addressing hit testing feedback raised previously by Jake Archibald, Stefan Zager proposed automatically applying a clipping rectangle to the hit test region for 2D canvas contexts, while requiring a Document Rectangle (`DOMRect`) to be passed into update geometry options for 3D and non-standard cases ([00:38:48](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.rkca0h3bah02)). Jake Archibald confirmed that the proposed clipping behavior aligned with expectations, and Philip Jägenstedt encouraged further review of both the readback-allowed rendering pull request and the main canvas pull request to advance to stage three ([00:40:13](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.dux0wjsn3r82)).
- Issue 10650 HTML and Canvas Attribute Naming: fantasai brought up concerns regarding the name `layout subtree` for making canvas contents drawable, proposing to reuse the term `content` with an enum value like `content equals drawable` (defaulting to `content equals fallback`) to leave room for future modes ([00:42:22](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.v5ttq88o4pbu)). Stephen Chenney and Simon Pieters discussed potential alternatives and whether future values are anticipated, while Lea Verou and Jake Archibald debated whether `content` is appropriate given that it usually declares content rather than capabilities ([00:43:47](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.88v4jem1df7x)). Johnny Stenback ultimately intervened to move the naming conversation to the pull requests due to time constraints ([00:47:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.xgfozgv2uz5u)).
- Module Import Link Tags Pull Request and Explainer Updates: Kurt Catti-Schmidt announced that module import link tags have been moved into a new pull request addressing earlier comments from Emilio, and requested reviews from Mozilla and WebKit participants ([00:47:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.xgfozgv2uz5u)). Lea Verou noted that a comment had just been left on the pull request, which Kurt Catti-Schmidt agreed to answer shortly. Additionally, Stefan Zager, Jake Archibald, and David Baron discussed process questions regarding when to update the explainer, reaching a consensus that explainers can be updated with current thinking and open discussion links once discussions around stage three become serious ([00:48:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1V4rMweWb4u1IR38gEdqFutkyKHrytMAvFty9egfjqZU/edit?userstoinvite=none&resourcekey=0-Q6pxDauVD0WSbd_zWSySAg&tab=t.o3p3m53mrnsw#heading=h.n5jgfn287v35)).
